## Embed a map

Place `bloomOutput()` in your UI and `renderBloom()` in the server. Nothing
needs to be added to the page's CSS or JavaScript.

```{r, eval=FALSE}
library(shiny)
library(bloomr)

ui <- fluidPage(
  bloomOutput("map", height = "520px"),
  textOutput("chosen")
)
server <- function(input, output, session) {
  output$map <- renderBloom({ bloom_map("nj") })
  output$chosen <- renderText({
    req(input$map_selected)
    paste(input$map_selected$name, input$map_selected$level)
  })
}
shinyApp(ui, server)
```

`input$map_selected` includes `id`, `geoid`, `name`, `level`, and `parent_id`.
Use these values to filter tables or update other charts. The input name uses
the map's output ID, so two maps can have separate selections.

## Update values without resetting the map

Create the widget once. When users change an indicator, update *only the
values* with a proxy. This keeps positions and animation state intact.

```{r, eval=FALSE}
observeEvent(input$metric, {
  bloom_update_data(
    bloomProxy("map"),
    data = county_data,
    key = "geoid",
    value = input$metric
  )
}, ignoreInit = TRUE)
```

`county_data` should have a character `geoid` column and numeric indicator
columns. The demo app supplies data and a working indicator selector:

```{r, eval=FALSE}
bloomr::run_bloom_example()
```

## Control the map from Shiny

```{r, eval=FALSE}
bloom_select(bloomProxy("map"), "bergen")
bloom_expand(bloomProxy("map"), "county")
bloom_reset(bloomProxy("map"))
```

Select a county first, then use `bloom_expand(..., "local")` to open it.
Commands run on the existing widget; do not re-render the widget for a change
in selection or indicators.

## Helpful integration notes

- The map is light by default and has styles scoped to its own container.
- Overview county boundaries and local municipality boundaries are visible
  by default; **Display** turns either off without resetting the map.
- Labels are off by default. Pass `labels = "selected"` or
  `labels = "custom", label_areas = c("bergen")` when needed.
- It can sit inside a dashboard card, a sidebar layout, or a Shiny tab.
- Give it an explicit height such as `height = "520px"`.
- No network access is needed for the bundled map data.
- `bloom_check_data()` checks columns, unique IDs, and missing values; it does
  not verify that every supplied ID matches a prepared boundary.
